Explore statistics on all named ski lifts in the world.
The table initially shows lifts that OpenSkiMap records as operating.
Clear the initial filter to inspect abandoned, proposed, and other lifts.
The underlying data is provided by [OpenSkiMap](https://openskimap.org) and [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org) with statistics computed by <https://github.com/dhimmel/openskistats>.

::: {.callout-caution}
OpenSkiStats is a work in progress.
Methods and results are subject to change.
Feedback is welcome via [GitHub issues](https://github.com/dhimmel/openskistats/issues/new).
:::

::: {.column-screen-inset}
<div
  data-oss-table="lifts"
  data-source="/data/lifts.json"
  aria-live="polite"
></div>
<script type="module" src="/common/table.bundle.js"></script>
:::

### Table usage

Numeric columns support these filters:

- `15` for value ≥ 15
- `-20` for value ≤ 20
- `[10, 20]` for 10 ≤ value ≤ 20
- `(10, 20)` for 10 < value < 20
- `(, 5]` for value ≤ 5

Text columns match any row containing what you type.
The ski-area filter matches any of the ski areas a lift serves.

`Ride` is the typical ride duration in minutes and seconds, and `Capacity` is the transport capacity in people per hour.
Both are recorded by OpenStreetMap contributors and are missing for many lifts.

### Source data

```{python}
from IPython.display import Markdown
from openskistats.openskimap_utils import load_openskimap_download_info

info = load_openskimap_download_info()["lifts"]
date_str = info.last_modified.split("T")[0]
Markdown(f"OpenSkiMap data is from {date_str}.")
```
